newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan January ethylene output up 4.8 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan January ethylene output up 4.8 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Japan's ethylene output in January rose 4.8 percent from a year ago to 655,000 tonnes, reflecting healthy demand from the domestic as well as the Asian market, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry said on Wednesday.
The January production, however, was down 1.9 percent from December, when ethylene output in Japan hit a record high of 668,000 tonnes.
The month-on-month decline was attributed to output cuts at some petrochemical firms in Japan.

Several ethylene manufacturers in Japan have started reducing ethylene output in an effort to raise wholesale prices for their petrochemical products, which have not followed the sharp rise in naphtha prices.
Near-term naphtha prices on Asia's benchmark open-specification forward contract shot up by about 33 percent in the second half of 1996 due to tight supplies as well as high global crude oil prices.

Mitsubishi Chemical Corp, Japan's largest petrochemical firm with an annual ethylene production capacity of 1.45 million tonnes, has been cutting its ethylene output by about 10 percent since January.
Another major manufacturer Showa Denko KK has also been reducing ethylene output by a few percent since late last year.
